quiz.q: You call `tracing::info!` everywhere but nothing prints. What's the most likely cause?
options: You need to restart your computer
No subscriber is installed — the macros emit events but nobody is listening
info! only works in release builds
quiz.explain: In tracing, macros only emit events. A separate subscriber (e.g. tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()) must be installed once at startup or nothing prints.

quiz.q: Which list shows log levels from least to most severe?
quiz.explain: From noisiest/least severe to most severe: trace, debug, info, warn, error. You set a threshold and everything below it is dropped.

quiz.q: Why prefer `info!(user_id = id, "logged in")` over `info!("user {id} logged in")`?
options: The value becomes a searchable structured field instead of unsearchable text
String formatting is not allowed in tracing
quiz.explain: Structured fields are labeled key/values that log tools can filter on (e.g. user_id = 7). Values glued into the message are just text.

quiz.q: What does a tracing `span` give you that a single `info!` event does not?
options: A duration of work whose context tags every log inside it (e.g. request_id)
quiz.explain: Events are single points; a span wraps a chunk of work so every log inside it carries shared context, letting you follow one request end to end.

flashcards.front: In the `tracing` crate, what actually decides where log events go?
flashcards.back: A subscriber. The info!/warn!/error! macros only emit events; you must install a subscriber (e.g. tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()) once at startup or nothing prints.

flashcards.front: Name the five log levels from least to most severe.
flashcards.back: trace, debug, info, warn, error. Set a threshold; everything below it is dropped.

flashcards.front: What is a structured field in tracing?
flashcards.back: A labeled key/value attached to a log event, e.g. info!(user_id = 7, "..."), that log tools can search and filter on — unlike text buried in the message.

flashcards.front: What is a span, and how does it differ from an event?
flashcards.back: A span represents a duration of work; every log inside it is tagged with the span's context (like request_id). Events are single points in time.
